description: lib/insecurity.ts's isRedirectAllowed checks url.includes(allowedUrl) for each entry in a small allowlist of trusted destinations, instead of checking that the target URL actually starts with (or equals the host of) an allowed entry. A URL on an attacker-controlled domain that merely contains an allowlisted string anywhere in its path or query, such as a query parameter whose value happens to be a trusted URL, passes this check and the server issues a real HTTP 302 redirect to the attacker's own domain.
expected_exploit_indicator: GET /redirect?to=<attacker domain>?x=<allowlisted URL> returns an HTTP 302 redirect whose Location header points at the attacker-controlled domain, not the allowlisted one
expected_blocked_signal: The same request is rejected (406) because the target URL does not actually start with any allowlisted origin
legitimate_check: A redirect straight to an allowlisted URL (no attacker-controlled host involved) still succeeds.
